### `whoami`

**Identify this credential.** Requires any valid key.

The workspace this API key acts in and the permissions it holds. Call this first when unsure what a key can do — the grant set is the same one every other tool is checked against.

**Input:** none

### `list_channels`

**List connected channels.** Requires `account:read`.

Every social account connected to the workspace, with its platform, handle and status. Returns a projection — access tokens are never part of it. Post-creating tools address channels by the `id` returned here.

**Input:** none

### `get_telegram_bot`

**Get the Telegram bot to add.** Requires any valid key.

The Telegram bot a channel must have as an administrator (with the Post Messages right) before connect_telegram_channel can connect it, plus a deep link that opens Telegram's add-as-admin picker with that right pre-selected. Adding the bot happens in Telegram, by a person — hand them the link.

**Input:** none

### `get_telegram_verification_code`

**Get a Telegram channel's verification code.** Requires `account:connect`.
Rate limited: 20 calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Check a Telegram channel is ready to connect (it exists, and the bot from get_telegram_bot is in it with Post Messages) and return the code its description must carry before connect_telegram_channel will connect it. Relay the code to the person to paste into the channel's description in Telegram; `verified: true` means it is already there and you can connect now.

**Input**

- `chat`: string (max length 256), required — The channel to connect: `@username`, a `t.me/username` link, or the numeric chat id for a private channel. The bot must already be an administrator of the channel with the Post Messages right, and the channel's description must carry this workspace's verification code — the first attempt without it is refused with the code to add.

### `connect_telegram_channel`

**Connect a Telegram channel.** Requires `account:connect`.
Rate limited: 20 calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Connect a Telegram channel or group as a posting channel. Two things must already be true, both done by a person in Telegram: the bot from get_telegram_bot is an administrator of the channel with Post Messages, and the channel's description contains this workspace's verification code. Get the code from get_telegram_verification_code first; a call without it in the description fails with a message carrying the code. The code can be removed once connected.

**Input**

- `chat`: string (max length 256), required — The channel to connect: `@username`, a `t.me/username` link, or the numeric chat id for a private channel. The bot must already be an administrator of the channel with the Post Messages right, and the channel's description must carry this workspace's verification code — the first attempt without it is refused with the code to add.

### `search_campaigns`

**Search campaigns.** Requires `campaign:read`.
Rate limited: 60 calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Campaigns whose name matches a query string.

**Input**

- `q`: string, required

### `list_posts`

**List posts.** Requires `post:read`.

What this workspace has — drafts, posts awaiting approval, scheduled posts and published ones — newest first, one entry per post however many channels it goes out on. Filter by `status`, `bucket` (the board column, where approval state outranks the lifecycle status), `platform`, `accountId`, `campaignId` and a `scheduledAfter`/`scheduledBefore` window; page with the `nextCursor` a page hands back. Use this to answer "what's going out this week?" or "what did we publish last month?" — `search_posts` is for finding one post by its words. For a single post's full content (threads, per-channel bodies, media) read it back with its `id`.

**Input**

- `limit`: integer (min 1, max 100, default 50)
- `cursor`: string
- `sort`: one of `"createdAt"` | `"scheduledAt"` (default "createdAt")
- `direction`: one of `"asc"` | `"desc"` (default "desc")
- `status`: array of one of `"draft"` | `"pending_approval"` | `"scheduled"` | `"publishing"` | `"published"` (min 1 items)
- `bucket`: array of one of `"drafts"` | `"needs_approval"` | `"needs_revision"` | `"approved"` | `"scheduled"` | `"posted"` (min 1 items)
- `platform`: array of string (min 1 items)
- `accountId`: array of string (min 1 items)
- `campaignId`: string
- `scheduledAfter`: string (date-time)
- `scheduledBefore`: string (date-time)
- `previewAccountId`: string

### `search_posts`

**Search posts.** Requires `post:read`.

Posts whose text matches a query, across drafts, scheduled and published. Each result carries its derived board bucket (drafts / needs approval / scheduled / published / failed).

**Input**

- `q`: string, required — Text to search for.

### `read_brand_voice`

**Read the brand voice.** Requires `brandVoice:read`.

The workspace's brand voice profile — tone, audience, rules and the distilled memo learned from published posts. Read this before drafting anything, so generated copy matches how this workspace already writes. Null when nothing has been configured yet.

**Input:** none

### `read_posting_schedule`

**Read the posting schedule.** Requires `postingSchedule:read`.

The weekly wall-clock times the workspace publishes at, and its timezone. With `accountId`, one channel's own schedule instead — where an empty slot list means that channel has nothing of its own and inherits the workspace's.

**Input**

- `accountId`: string

### `suggest_post_times`

**Suggest when to post.** Requires `postingSchedule:read`.

Candidate publish times, one entry per channel. Call this before create_post unless the caller named a time: the slot strategies return the workspace's configured posting slots that nothing is scheduled on yet, which is the only way to place a post without booking a slot that already holds one — read_posting_schedule shows the times but not which are taken.

`first-available` (the default) takes the soonest free slot; `queue` appends after everything already booked, so a batch keeps its order; `best-time` ignores the schedule and ranks a per-platform engagement profile instead. That profile is a static heuristic, not measured analytics for this account — `researched` says whether the platform has a profile of its own or the generic fallback, and neither should be described to a person as data about their audience.

An empty `times` means the channel has no free slot in the next two weeks.

**Input**

- `accountIds`: array of string (min 1 items, max 50 items)
- `strategy`: one of `"first-available"` | `"queue"` | `"best-time"` (default "first-available")
- `count`: integer (min 1, max 10, default 1)
- `after`: string (date-time)

### `create_tag`

**Create a tag.** Requires `tag:create`.

Create a workspace tag. Names are unique per workspace, case-insensitively — creating one that already exists is a conflict, not a silent no-op.

**Input**

- `name`: string (max length 60), required
- `color`: one of `"grey"` | `"dark-grey"` | `"purple"` | `"blue"` | `"teal"` | `"green"` | `"yellow"` | `"orange"` | `"pink"` | `"red"` (default "grey")

### `create_campaign`

**Create a campaign.** Requires `campaign:create`.

Create an empty campaign (a title, and optionally a colour, icon, dates and description). Posts join it afterwards by passing its id as `info.campaignId` on create_post or save_draft.

**Input**

- `title`: string (max length 200), required
- `color`: one of `"grey"` | `"dark-grey"` | `"purple"` | `"blue"` | `"teal"` | `"green"` | `"yellow"` | `"orange"` | `"pink"` | `"red"`
- `icon`: string | null
- `startDate`: string (date-time) | null
- `endDate`: string (date-time) | null
- `description`: string (max length 4000, default "")

### `upload_media`

**Upload an image or video.** Requires `media:create`.

Store bytes you already hold. Returns a record whose `id` is what you put in an item's `mediaIds` on create_post or save_draft. Use this for an image you generated or were given — anything you have as data rather than as a public URL. `dataBase64` is standard base64 of the file itself (a data: prefix is tolerated). Images, video and PDF only, up to 10MB decoded.

**Input**

- `name`: string (max length 255), required
- `mimeType`: string (max length 255), required
- `dataBase64`: string, required
- `altText`: string (max length 2000)

### `upload_media_from_url`

**Upload media from a URL.** Requires `media:create`.

Fetch a publicly reachable URL and store it. Returns a record whose `id` goes in an item's `mediaIds`. Cheaper than upload_media when the file is already on the web — the bytes never pass through the conversation. The URL must be publicly resolvable; private and internal addresses are refused.

**Input**

- `url`: string (uri), required
- `name`: string (max length 255)
- `altText`: string (max length 2000)

### `save_draft`

**Save a draft.** Requires `post:create`.

Create or replace a draft. With `groupId` the existing draft is replaced wholesale (that is the composer's autosave semantics — every editable row is deleted and re-inserted, preserving status, per-account fire times and the approval gate); without one a new draft is created. To attach an image or video, first call upload_media or upload_media_from_url, then put the returned id in that item's `mediaIds`. To edit an existing post, get_post it first and send the whole `accounts` array back with its `groupId`.

### `create_post`

**Schedule or publish a post.** Requires `post:create`.

Create posts on one or more channels. `scheduledAt` is an ISO 8601 instant; `publishNow: true` sends it as soon as possible instead. Synced accounts are grouped as one logical post, each unsynced account gets its own. To attach an image or video, first call upload_media (bytes you hold) or upload_media_from_url (a public URL), then put the returned id in that item's `mediaIds`.

Publishing is handed to the background worker rather than run here, so `publishNow` means 'published within about a minute', not 'published by the time this returns'. Call get_publish_status with the returned `groupIds` to see the outcome, and get_post to read back what was created.

To route the post through review, pass `approval` with `reviewerIds` from list_members and a `blocking` choice (ask the person whether the post should wait for approval or publish on schedule regardless, if they haven't said) — the request is created in the same transaction, and reviewers are told in-app and on the workspace's Slack/Discord routes (email goes out only when asked from the app). An author without publish authority must do this to schedule at all.

- `scheduledAt`: string (date-time), required
- `accounts`: array of object (min 1 items), required
  - `accountId`: string, required
  - `items`: array of object, required
    - `id`: string, required
    - `content`: string, required

      - `reaction`: one of `"LIKE"` | `"LOVE"` | `"CELEBRATE"` | `"INSIGHTFUL"` | `"CURIOUS"` | `"SUPPORT"`
    - `repost`: object, required
      - `enabled`: boolean, required
      - `entries`: array of object (default [])
        - `fromAccountId`: string, required

      - `delayMinutes`: integer (min 0, max 10080)
      - `fromAccountId`: string | null
    - `slack`: object
      - `enabled`: boolean, required
      - `entries`: array of object (default [])

        - `items`: array of object (default [])

    - `discord`: object

        - `items`: array of object (default [])

          - `poll`: object
  - `replySettings`: one of `"everyone"` | `"following"` | `"mentionedUsers"` | `"subscribers"` | `"verified"` | `"accounts_you_follow"` | `"mentioned_only"` | `"followers_only"` | `"parent_post_author_only"`
  - `postFormat`: one of `"post"` | `"story"` | `"reel"`
  - `platformOptions`: object
    - `tiktok`: object
      - `title`: string (max length 2200)
      - `privacyLevel`: one of `"PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE"` | `"MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS"` | `"FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR"` | `"SELF_ONLY"`
      - `disableComment`: boolean
      - `disableDuet`: boolean

- `replaceGroupId`: string
- `publishNow`: boolean
- `info`: object
  - `title`: string (max length 200)
  - `tags`: array of string (max 50 items)
  - `tagColors`: object
  - `campaignId`: string | null
- `approval`: object
  - `reviewerIds`: array of string (min 1 items), required
  - `message`: string | null
  - `dueDate`: string (date-time) | null
  - `requireAll`: boolean (default false)
  - `blocking`: boolean, required — Required. `true` (blocking): the post will not publish until the request is approved. `false` (non-blocking): the post publishes on schedule, and the review is advisory. If the person has not said which, ask them with these two options rather than choosing. An author without publish authority always gets a blocking request, so pass `true` for them. On `intent: "edit"`, pass the request's current value (get_approval) unless the person asked to change it.
  - `publishOnApprove`: boolean (default false)

### `get_post`

**Read one post in full.** Requires `post:read`.

The whole post by id: every channel's items (text, media, poll, quote, reply-to, link preview), per-channel settings, fire time, title, tags, campaign, and both approval states. This is the read list_posts deliberately isn't — call it before editing (save_draft replaces the whole `accounts` array, so you need the current one) and after creating, to confirm what landed.

`status` is the group's real lifecycle state: `draft`, `scheduled`, `pending_approval`, `publishing`, `published`, `failed`, or `mixed` when its channels have diverged. Unlike the app's own open path, reading never changes anything — a failed post stays failed until you act on it.

`approvalStatus` is what a reviewer sees (the active request, blocking or not); `approvalGateStatus` is what actually stands between the post and the worker.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.

### `get_publish_status`

**Check publish progress.** Requires `post:read`.

Per-channel publish outcome for one or more posts: each account's status, its error or warning when there is one, and once published the live `platformUrl` on the network plus the network's own `platformPostId`. `done` is true once every channel has reached a terminal state. This is how you find out what happened after create_post with `publishNow` or after publish_post — both hand the work to the background worker and return before it runs.

**Input**

- `groupIds`: array of string (min 1 items, max 50 items), required

### `schedule_post`

**Schedule a post, or move its time.** Requires `post:update`.

Set when a post fires. On a draft this is the step from saved to scheduled — the content already stored is what goes out, so there is nothing to resend — and it must have some content to schedule. On a scheduled or pending-approval post the whole group shifts to the new time, keeping any per-channel stagger relative. `scheduledAt` must be in the future. Use suggest_post_times to pick a slot that isn't already taken.

A draft whose author can't publish is scheduled behind the approval gate exactly as the app would do it: it fires once a reviewer approves.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.
- `scheduledAt`: string (date-time), required — ISO 8601 instant, strictly in the future.

### `publish_post`

**Publish a post now.** Requires `post:update`.

Send a draft or scheduled post as soon as possible, using the content already stored. Needs publish authority: an author who must request approval is refused, and a post whose blocking approval is still pending or rejected is refused too — the worker would never claim it.

Like create_post's `publishNow`, this queues the post for the background worker rather than publishing inline, so it means 'within about a minute'. Follow up with get_publish_status.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.

### `unschedule_post`

**Move a post back to draft.** Requires `post:update`.

Take a scheduled or pending-approval post off the calendar and return it to draft, keeping its content. An unresolved blocking approval keeps gating the draft; an already-approved one is dissolved so the post lands as a plain draft. `removeApproval: true` dissolves the request regardless, and needs publish authority.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.
- `removeApproval`: boolean — Also dissolve the group's approval request, landing the post as a plain (ungated) draft. Needs publish authority.

### `delete_post`

**Delete a draft or scheduled post.** Requires `post:delete`.

Discard a post that hasn't gone out — draft, scheduled or pending approval. Refused once any channel is publishing, published or failed: removing a live post from the networks is a different operation this server doesn't perform.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.

### `update_post_info`

**Update a post's title, tags or campaign.** Requires `post:update`.

Metadata only — the content and schedule are untouched, so this is safe on scheduled and published posts. Fields you omit are left as they are; `campaignId: null` removes the post from its campaign. Tags are created by name if they don't exist yet.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.
- `title`: string (max length 200)
- `tags`: array of string (max 50 items)
- `tagColors`: object
- `campaignId`: string | null

### `list_members`

**List workspace members.** Requires `member:read`.

Everyone in the workspace with their role. The `userId` values are what request_approval takes as `reviewerIds`, and what a member's name resolves to in activity and comments.

**Input:** none

### `get_approval`

**Read a post's approval request.** Requires `approval:read`.

The live approval request on a post, or null when there is none: status, whether it blocks publishing, whether every reviewer must approve, the due date, and each reviewer with their decision so far.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.

### `request_approval`

**Request review of a post.** Requires `approval:request`.

Ask named teammates to approve a post before it publishes, or edit an existing request's roster, message and due date (`intent: "edit"`). `reviewerIds` are member `userId`s from list_members. `blocking` is required: `true` holds the post at the publish gate until approved, `false` lets it publish on schedule with the review as advice. When the person hasn't said which, ask them to choose between those two before calling. An author without publish authority always gets a blocking request whatever they pass. `requireAll` needs every reviewer's approval rather than the first.

New reviewers are notified in-app and on the workspace's Slack/Discord routes; the reviewer email is only sent when the request is made from the app.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.
- `intent`: one of `"create"` | `"edit"` (default "create")
- `reviewerIds`: array of string (min 1 items), required
- `message`: string | null
- `dueDate`: string (date-time) | null
- `requireAll`: boolean (default false)
- `blocking`: boolean, required — Required. `true` (blocking): the post will not publish until the request is approved. `false` (non-blocking): the post publishes on schedule, and the review is advisory. If the person has not said which, ask them with these two options rather than choosing. An author without publish authority always gets a blocking request, so pass `true` for them. On `intent: "edit"`, pass the request's current value (get_approval) unless the person asked to change it.

### `decide_approval`

**Approve or reject a post.** Requires `approval:decide`.

Record a decision on a post's approval request. `comment` is the note that goes back to whoever asked — on a rejection it is the reason, so say what should change. Only a named reviewer or a holder of approval:decide may decide, never the post's own author unless they could have published it themselves. On a require-all request one approval is a vote, not the outcome: `resolvesRequest` says whether this decision settled it. Approving a blocking request releases the post to publish at its scheduled time.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.
- `decision`: one of `"approved"` | `"rejected"`, required
- `comment`: string | null

### `remove_approval`

**Withdraw a post's approval request.** Requires `approval:request`.

Remove the request entirely, which opens the publish gate — so it needs publish authority, the same as approving would. An author who can't publish cannot withdraw their own request; a reviewer has to decide it.

**Input**

- `groupId`: string, required — The post's id — `groupId` from create_post, save_draft or list_posts.

### `list_conversations`

**List inbox conversations.** Requires `inbox:read`.

Replies and mentions across the workspace's channels, newest activity first. Filter by `status` (open / resolved / snoozed), `platform`, `type` (reply / mention), `accountId`, `postId`, `assignee` (`unassigned` or a teammate's user id) or `inboxId` (a team inbox). Cursor-paged: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Snoozes that have come due are woken before the list is read, so `open` is always current.

**Input**

- `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"`
- `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"`
- `postId`: string
- `accountId`: string
- `assignee`: string
- `inboxId`: string
- `status`: one of `"open"` | `"resolved"` | `"snoozed"`
- `cursor`: string
- `limit`: integer (min 1, max 100)

### `get_conversation`

**Read a conversation thread.** Requires `inbox:read`.

One conversation with its full message thread — the post it hangs off, the participant, and every message in order. Read this before deciding how to triage; list_conversations carries only the latest message.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.

### `count_conversations`

**Count the conversations in a view.** Requires `inbox:read`.

How many conversations a view holds — the number on the inbox's badges. Takes the same filters as list_conversations (`type`, `platform`, `accountId`, `postId`, `assignee`, `inboxId`), plus `status` (open by default). `unread: true` narrows to the ones whose latest message nobody in the workspace has read, which is a different question from how much is still open.

**Input**

- `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"`
- `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"`
- `postId`: string
- `accountId`: string
- `assignee`: string
- `inboxId`: string
- `status`: one of `"open"` | `"resolved"` | `"snoozed"`
- `unread`: boolean

### `resolve_conversation`

**Resolve a conversation.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Mark a conversation handled. Resolving clears any pending snooze. Status is shared workspace state — everyone sees it resolved.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.

### `reopen_conversation`

**Reopen a conversation.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Return a resolved or snoozed conversation to the open list.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.

### `snooze_conversation`

**Snooze a conversation.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Hide a conversation until `until` (ISO 8601, strictly in the future), when it returns to the open list as unread.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.
- `until`: string (date-time), required — When to bring it back.

### `mark_conversation_read`

**Mark a conversation read.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Advance the workspace's read watermark on a conversation to now. Read state is shared, not per person.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.

### `mark_conversation_unread`

**Mark a conversation unread.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Clear the read watermark so the latest incoming message counts as unread again — the way to flag something for a teammate.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.

### `resolve_all_conversations`

**Resolve or reopen every conversation in a status.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Move every conversation currently in `from` to `to` — 'resolve everything open', or 'reopen everything resolved'. Takes the same filters as list_conversations (`type`, `platform`, `accountId`, `postId`, `assignee`, `inboxId`) and moves exactly the conversations that list would return; with none it sweeps the whole workspace. Returns how many moved. Read the list first with the same filters if the sweep is at all selective.

**Input**

- `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"`
- `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"`
- `postId`: string
- `accountId`: string
- `assignee`: string
- `inboxId`: string
- `from`: one of `"open"` | `"resolved"` | `"snoozed"`, required
- `to`: one of `"open"` | `"resolved"`, required

### `snooze_all_conversations`

**Snooze every conversation in a status.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Snooze every conversation currently in `from` until the same future instant. Scoped by the list_conversations filters exactly as resolve_all_conversations is.

**Input**

- `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"`
- `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"`
- `postId`: string
- `accountId`: string
- `assignee`: string
- `inboxId`: string
- `from`: one of `"open"` | `"resolved"` | `"snoozed"`, required
- `until`: string, required

### `reply_to_conversation`

**Reply in a conversation.** Requires `inbox:reply` or `approval:request`.
Rate limited: 30 calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Answer a reply or mention on the platform it came from. Answers the reply or mention the conversation was opened for, or the message named by `replyToMessageId` (a message id from get_conversation). `text` may be empty when `media` carries an attachment. Read get_conversation first — a reply without the thread's context reads like one.

What comes back depends on the key. With `inbox:reply` the reply is published and `status` is `sent`, with the updated thread. Without it (but with `approval:request`) nothing is published: the reply is held for someone who can approve it, `status` is `held`, and the approvers are told — list_held_replies shows where it got to. Replies are published as the channel's account, so write in the workspace's voice (read_brand_voice).

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.
- `text`: string (default "")
- `replyToMessageId`: string | null — Reply to a specific comment (its message id). Omit to reply to the post.
- `media`: array of object — Optional attachments (e.g. a GIF)
  - `url`: string, required
  - `mimeType`: string, required
  - `altText`: string
  - `sourceUrl`: string
  - `videoUrl`: string
  - `width`: number
  - `height`: number
  - `bytes`: number

### `assign_conversation`

**Assign a conversation.** Requires `inbox:update`.

Give a conversation an owner, or hand it back to the shared pool with `assigneeUserId: null`. Owners are teammates' `userId`s from list_members (list_team_availability shows who is away or already busy). Ownership is shared triage state, and changing it is recorded in the audit log.

**Input**

- `conversationId`: string, required — A conversation id from list_conversations.
- `assigneeUserId`: string | null, required — A member's userId, or null to unassign.

### `sync_inbox`

**Pull new replies from the platforms.** Requires `inbox:update`.
Rate limited: 6 matching calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Fetch replies and mentions the platforms have that the inbox doesn't yet. The inbox already syncs in the background every ten minutes, so only call this when something is known to be missing. Skipped (`skipped: true`) when a sync ran in the last two minutes; `force: true` overrides that, but spends the platforms' metered read budget (X reads are billed) — use it sparingly.

**Input**

- `force`: boolean

### `list_held_replies`

**List replies waiting for approval.** Requires `approval:read`.

Replies drafted by someone who can't publish directly, held until an approver releases them — newest first, with who drafted each, its text, and where it stands (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `sent`, `failed`). `decidable: true` is what decide_held_reply will accept: a pending reply, a failed send, or an approval whose send never finished. Filter with `statuses` (e.g. `["pending"]` for the queue).

**Input**

- `statuses`: array of one of `"pending"` | `"approved"` | `"rejected"` | `"sent"` | `"failed"`

### `decide_held_reply`

**Approve or reject a held reply.** Requires `approval:decide`.
Rate limited: 30 matching calls per 60s, shared with the HTTP route for the same operation.

Release a held reply to its platform (`approve`), release it with your own wording (`edit_approve`, with the replacement in `body`), or turn it down (`reject`, with the reason in `note` — the drafter is told). Approving publishes: `status: sent` means it is live; `send_failed` means the decision stands but the send failed, and deciding again retries it — unless the error says the send couldn't be confirmed, in which case read the conversation first: it may already be live. You can't approve a reply attributed to this key's own creator unless the key could have replied directly.

**Input**

- `pendingReplyId`: string, required — A held reply's id from list_held_replies.
- `action`: one of `"approve"` | `"edit_approve"` | `"reject"`, required
- `body`: string
- `note`: string

### `get_inbox_assignment`

**Read how conversations are assigned.** Requires `teamInbox:read`.

How the workspace hands out every conversation no team inbox claims: `method` (`manual` leaves them unassigned, `round_robin` rotates, `balanced` picks whoever has the fewest open), who is in the rotation (`allMembers`, or `members`), and how many conversations are waiting for an owner — `waitingInManual` says which of those sit in a manual inbox, which distribute_waiting_conversations can't assign.

**Input:** none

### `update_inbox_assignment`

**Change how conversations are assigned.** Requires `teamInbox:update`.

Set the workspace's assignment `method`, who's in the rotation (`allMembers: true`, or `members` — replacing the list), whether round robin keeps assigning to people who are away (`rrAssignWhenAway`), and a `wrapUpMinutes` pause after someone resolves a conversation. Fields you omit are left as they are. Applies to conversations as they arrive; call distribute_waiting_conversations for the ones already waiting.

**Input**

- `method`: one of `"manual"` | `"round_robin"` | `"balanced"`
- `allMembers`: boolean
- `members`: array of object (max 200 items)
  - `userId`: string, required
  - `tier`: one of `"primary"` | `"secondary"`
  - `capacity`: integer | null
  - `skills`: array of string | null
- `rrAssignWhenAway`: boolean
- `wrapUpMinutes`: integer (min 0, max 240)

### `distribute_waiting_conversations`

**Assign the waiting backlog.** Requires `teamInbox:update`.

Hand out conversations already waiting without an owner, oldest first, through the same routing a new arrival gets (each is re-matched against today's team inbox sources). Routing only decides a conversation as it arrives, so this is how a backlog from before assignment was set up gets owners. Up to 500 a call; `waiting` says how many are still unowned afterwards.

**Input:** none

### `list_team_inboxes`

**List team inboxes.** Requires `teamInbox:read`.

The team inboxes carved out of the workspace inbox, in the order routing checks them: each with its sources (which conversations it claims — by channel, platform, type or keywords), its members, and its assignment method. A new conversation goes to the first inbox with a matching source, otherwise to the workspace's own assignment. Pass an inbox's `id` as `inboxId` to list_conversations to see what it holds.

**Input:** none

### `create_team_inbox`

**Create a team inbox.** Requires `teamInbox:create`.

Carve a team inbox out of the workspace inbox. `sources` decide what it claims — each needs at least one condition (`accountId` from list_channels, `platform`, `type`, or any-of `keywords`) and every condition in a source must match. `members` are teammates from list_members, `primary` or `secondary` (secondaries take overflow when primaries are away or full). It goes last in the routing order; reorder with reorder_team_inboxes.

**Input**

- `name`: string (max length 120), required
- `description`: string | null
- `method`: one of `"manual"` | `"round_robin"` | `"balanced"`
- `skillsEnabled`: boolean
- `awayReassign`: boolean
- `rrAssignWhenAway`: boolean
- `wrapUpMinutes`: integer (min 0, max 240)
- `sources`: array of object (max 50 items)
  - `accountId`: string | null
  - `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"` | null
  - `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"` | null
  - `keywords`: array of string | null
- `members`: array of object (max 200 items)
  - `userId`: string, required
  - `tier`: one of `"primary"` | `"secondary"`
  - `capacity`: integer | null
  - `skills`: array of string | null

### `update_team_inbox`

**Change a team inbox.** Requires `teamInbox:update`.

Edit a team inbox. Fields you omit are left as they are; `sources` and `members`, when given, replace the whole list — read it with list_team_inboxes first.

**Input**

- `inboxId`: string, required — A team inbox id from list_team_inboxes.
- `name`: string (max length 120)
- `description`: string | null
- `method`: one of `"manual"` | `"round_robin"` | `"balanced"`
- `skillsEnabled`: boolean
- `awayReassign`: boolean
- `rrAssignWhenAway`: boolean
- `wrapUpMinutes`: integer (min 0, max 240)
- `sources`: array of object (max 50 items)
  - `accountId`: string | null
  - `platform`: one of `"bluesky"` | `"twitter"` | `"threads"` | `"mastodon"` | `"facebook_page"` | `"instagram"` | `"linkedin_page"` | null
  - `type`: one of `"reply"` | `"mention"` | null
  - `keywords`: array of string | null
- `members`: array of object (max 200 items)
  - `userId`: string, required
  - `tier`: one of `"primary"` | `"secondary"`
  - `capacity`: integer | null
  - `skills`: array of string | null

### `delete_team_inbox`

**Delete a team inbox.** Requires `teamInbox:delete`.

Remove a team inbox. Its conversations are kept and count as the workspace inbox's from then on; their owners are unchanged.

**Input**

- `inboxId`: string, required — A team inbox id from list_team_inboxes.

### `reorder_team_inboxes`

**Set the routing order.** Requires `teamInbox:update`.

The order routing checks team inboxes in — the first one with a matching source wins. `inboxIds` must name every team inbox exactly once.

**Input**

- `inboxIds`: array of string (max 200 items), required

### `list_team_availability`

**Who's available in the inbox.** Requires `inboxStatus:read`.

Every teammate with their inbox status (`active`, `away`, or `away_reassign`, which also hands their open conversations back), whether it was set automatically after inactivity (`autoAway`), and how many open conversations they own (`openCount`). Check this before assigning.

**Input:** none

### `set_teammate_status`

**Set a teammate's inbox status.** Requires `inboxStatus:manageAny`.

Mark a teammate `active`, `away` (no new conversations are routed to them), or `away_reassign` (away, and their open conversations are handed back out now). An API key has no status of its own, so `userId` (from list_members) is required and this is an override of that person's own setting.

**Input**

- `userId`: string, required — The teammate's userId from list_members.
- `status`: one of `"active"` | `"away"` | `"away_reassign"`, required

### `get_inbox_settings`

**Read the inbox settings.** Requires `teamInbox:read`.

Workspace-wide inbox defaults: how many open conversations a teammate carries before balanced assignment skips them (`defaultMemberCapacity`), after how many idle minutes someone is marked away automatically, whether that pauses their assignments, and how a teammate opening a conversation someone else is on is handled (`collisionHandling`).

**Input:** none

### `update_inbox_settings`

**Change the inbox settings.** Requires `teamInbox:update`.

Change any of the workspace-wide inbox defaults get_inbox_settings reads. Fields you omit are left as they are.

**Input**

- `defaultMemberCapacity`: integer (min 1, max 1000)
- `autoAwayThresholdMinutes`: integer (min 1, max 1440)
- `autoAwayPausesAssignment`: boolean
- `collisionHandling`: one of `"off"` | `"warn"` | `"soft_lock"`

### `list_channel_posting_schedules`

**Posting slots per channel.** Requires `postingSchedule:read`.

Every connected channel with the weekly slots it publishes on, kept separate rather than collapsed — what a queue needs to know which times are *this* channel's. A channel with no slots of its own inherits the workspace's, and is shown with them. Times are (dayOfWeek, minuteOfDay) in the channel's timezone.

**Input:** none

### `set_posting_schedule`

**Replace the posting schedule.** Requires `postingSchedule:update`.

Rewrite the weekly slots — for one channel with `accountId`, or for every channel (and as the default for channels connected later) without it. `mode: "smart"` spreads `frequencyPerWeek` slots across the week; `mode: "manual"` takes an explicit `slots` grid of times × days (Monday first). `timezone` is an IANA zone. Replaces rather than adds: re-running with the same input is a no-op in effect.

**Input**

- `accountId`: string
- `mode`: one of `"smart"` | `"manual"` (default "smart")
- `frequencyPerWeek`: number (max 100, default 1)
- `slots`: array of object (max 50 items)
  - `time`: string, required
  - `days`: array of boolean (max 7 items), required
- `timezone`: string (max length 100)

### `update_tag`

**Rename or recolour a tag.** Requires `tag:update`.

Change a tag's name and colour. Posts follow automatically — they link by id. Renaming onto a name that already exists (case-insensitively) is a conflict.

**Input**

- `tagId`: string, required — A tag id from list_tags.
- `name`: string (max length 60), required
- `color`: one of `"grey"` | `"dark-grey"` | `"purple"` | `"blue"` | `"teal"` | `"green"` | `"yellow"` | `"orange"` | `"pink"` | `"red"`, required

### `delete_tag`

**Delete a tag.** Requires `tag:delete`.

Remove a tag from the workspace and from every post carrying it. The posts themselves are untouched.

**Input**

- `tagId`: string, required — A tag id from list_tags.

### `list_media`

**List the media library.** Requires `media:read`.

The workspace's uploaded images, videos and PDFs, newest first, with `total` and a `nextOffset` for paging. Any `pending` record is checked against storage as it's read, so an upload that has landed reports `uploaded` without a separate confirmation. Externally hosted media (a GIF picked from GIPHY) has no record here.

**Input**

- `offset`: integer (min 0, max 9007199254740991, default 0)
- `limit`: integer (min 1, max 100, default 50)

### `get_media`

**Read one media record.** Requires `media:read`.

One library record by id: URL, type, size, dimensions or duration, alt text, and whether the bytes have landed.

**Input**

- `mediaId`: string, required — A media id from upload_media, upload_media_from_url or list_media.

### `delete_media`

**Delete a media record and its file.** Requires `media:delete`.

Remove the record and the stored object. Posts already carrying the file keep working — attaching copies the URL into the post — but the URL stops serving once the CDN's cached copy expires, so a scheduled post that still has to fetch it at publish time will fail then. Check list_posts before deleting something recent. If the stored object can't be removed the record is kept, so the delete can be retried.

**Input**

- `mediaId`: string, required — A media id from upload_media, upload_media_from_url or list_media.

### `get_media_usage`

**Media uploads this month.** Requires `media:read`.

How many files and bytes the workspace has uploaded this UTC calendar month. Uploads are metered rather than capped today; this is the number a plan limit would be judged on.

**Input:** none
